acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks seed rows, UNIQUE and CHECK rejections, nullable column, index, and seeded item mapping against migrations/0003.
test/index.test.js 'AC-2': title-only insert gives null category_id; category_id 999 fails with FOREIGN KEY.
'AC-3' test checks id order, labelled markup and unlabelled <li>; src/index.js item() matches the spec markup.
'AC-4' asserts link order (All, then case-insensitive name order), hrefs, a single aria-current on All, and an empty category's link.
Two 'AC-5' tests: Work-only items in id order, Work current, and extra params identical to the base pages.
'AC-6' test: 200, 'No items in this category.', no <li>, links shown with Garden current.
'AC-7' test adds 'R&D <x>', checks the escaped label, the encoded href, and that following the href lists the item.
it.each 'AC-8' covers all five bad links: 404, message, Go back href '/', referrer script, no <li> and no <nav>.
'AC-9' test checks HEAD status for /, /?category=Work (200) and /?category=Wrok (404).

The spec gives a concrete browser procedure. I read the inline script in src/index.js brokenLinkPage: it goes back only for a same-origin referrer, otherwise the link's href '/' applies. That matches the spec. I did not run a browser.

routes.json lists /?category=Work. tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers query accepted and whitespace, '#' and no-slash rejected. test/traffic.test.js records path plus query and checks ROUTES. index.test.js 'AC-11' hits each route and expects 2xx. traffic/src/index.js passes the path with its query through.

The existing healthz, 404, 405, escaping and empty-table tests are retained. The
  • First item
    • assertion is updated to the AC-3 markup; the other handlers are unchanged.
test/apply-migrations.js drops all tables in one batch with defer_foreign_keys. The suite would fail in beforeEach if the reset broke; the 'AC-13' test only weakly proves it.

findings.what: The AC-13 test adds a row and expects a count of 4. It would pass with any reset that restores the seed, and it does not check the foreign key is enforced. A broken reset would be caught by beforeEach failing, not by this test.
findings.fix: Optionally also assert that PRAGMA foreign_key_list(items) lists categories, or that an orphan insert fails, after the reset.

lenses.note: The change matches the owner's ask (a category per item and a list filter), and the spec records the owner's go dated before the implementation commits. No scope was added.

All 13 items are met, and every State-table row has a test: the '/' with items, '/' with no items, known category with items, known category with none, and broken-link rows. The spec edits all precede the go commit, and no acceptance item was edited after it.
Tests name their AC ids and assert behaviour. I could not run npm test here because vitest is not installed; CI covers that. No tests were deleted or loosened.
README updated for the filter and the 404 behaviour.
The query is parameterised, the match is exact, the HEAD status equals GET, and repeated or empty values are handled.
Names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded, SQL uses bound parameters, and no planted instructions were found.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page changed. There is no stylesheet or UI component, and the spec has no design requirements.
No browser or UI harness is available here. AC-10 was reviewed by reading the script, not run.
